china_race_dynamics.text:
Today I joined organizers, researchers, workers, and community leaders at the Community-Centered AI Infrastructure Summit @CarnegieMellon  to talk about what AI innovations should look like in Pennsylvania.

Leading on AI doesn’t mean more data centers at any cost or an arms race to superintelligence. It means making sure that AI actually improves life for all of us, not just CEOs and oligarchs.

We have a collective responsibility to ensure that. We need strong regulations to protect our civil rights, workplace, democracy, environment, and our health.

deepseek.reason: The speaker rejects the idea that leading on AI means an arms race to superintelligence.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Race skepticism is explicit, though the statement does not mention China directly.

astra.reason: The speaker rejects an arms race to superintelligence without connecting that race to competition with China.
astra.confidence_reason: The statement concerns general AI development priorities rather than US–China competition.
